learningObjective: Apply the Roofline model to classify a batch-1 GEMV as compute- or memory-bound on a specific GPU and derive the achievable throughput ceiling from arithmetic intensity times HBM bandwidth.

canonicalClaims.claim: A batch-1 GEMV that streams its weight matrix from HBM has arithmetic intensity around 1 FLOP/byte and is memory-bound whenever the target GPU's ridge point exceeds 1 FLOP/byte.
conditions: Weights loaded exactly once from HBM (no persistent-kernel or weight caching that changes reuse).
Ridge point (peak compute / peak HBM BW) is much larger than 1 FLOP/byte.
Kernel is FP16 or FP32 without exotic weight-only compression that changes bytes moved.
nonImplications: Does not imply the ceiling is exactly HBM BW in FLOP/s; the ceiling is HBM BW × AI.
Does not imply that a batched GEMM (multiple x vectors) is also memory-bound: batching raises AI proportionally.

sourceMappings.locator: Ch. 4, memory-bandwidth-bound regime of DL kernels

canonicalClaims.claim: The Roofline ceiling for a memory-bound kernel equals arithmetic intensity multiplied by peak HBM bandwidth.
conditions: Kernel does not saturate on-chip caches such that HBM traffic drops significantly.
AI is measured against HBM traffic, not L1/SMEM traffic.
nonImplications: Does not imply that achievable throughput equals ceiling; real kernels usually fall below.

misconceptions.claim: Batch-1 GEMV can approach the FP16 Tensor Core compute peak because the underlying kernel uses Tensor Cores.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Using Tensor Cores does not raise arithmetic intensity; the weight matrix still must be streamed once from HBM, capping throughput at HBM × AI regardless of compute hardware used.

misconceptions.claim: Because on-chip SRAM has much higher bandwidth than HBM, the Roofline ceiling for a streaming GEMV is set by SRAM bandwidth.
misconceptions.whyWrong: SRAM (shared memory / L1) only affects kernels that reuse data across many operations from cache; for a single pass over weights, HBM bandwidth is the binding constraint.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA Best Practices Guide, memory hierarchy discussion

misconceptions.claim: Arithmetic intensity for GEMV y=Wx is around 2 FLOP/byte because each multiply-add is 2 FLOPs per weight and each weight is 1 byte.
misconceptions.whyWrong: This ignores the FP16 (2 bytes) dtype of weights and off-by-a-factor. AI is (2·N·N) / (2·N·N + small) ≈ 1 FLOP/byte for FP16 weights, not 2.

misconceptions.claim: Since the GPU has 65 K registers per SM, a batch-1 GEMV is register-pressure limited rather than bandwidth limited.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Register pressure affects occupancy, not the absolute HBM-bound ceiling; a bandwidth-limited kernel can be run at low occupancy without further slowdown.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA C++ Programming Guide, occupancy and register file

implementationFacts: For square N=K FP16, AI = 2·N·N / (2·N·N + O(N)·2) ≈ 1 FLOP/byte
performanceScenarios: Weight streaming for a single decode step in a transformer (each linear layer is a GEMV) is HBM-bandwidth limited, motivating weight quantization and weight caching.
